EXECUTED ANALYSIS COMPLETE — RESULT

HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded; outcome limitation kept prominent):
In the NLSY79 data, individuals from higher-SES families (each additional year of parental schooling, higher pre-college family income) and, to a weaker degree, racial/ethnic cohort membership are strongly associated with college attendance/completion proxied by dormitory residence. These associations are substantially, but not entirely, statistical artifacts of academic characteristics: adding ASVAB achievement scores (and class-rank percentile) to a baseline SES+race logistic model attenuates the parental-education and income coefficients by roughly 30–60% and drives the small negative cohort-1 (Black-coded) coefficient to essentially zero, while the cohort-2 (Hispanic-coded) advantage persists and even strengthens after academic controls. Thus, academic achievement appears to be the main channel through which SES relates to (proxied) BA attainment, and the residual race gap after accounting for academics runs in the opposite direction for the Hispanic-coded group — conditional on equal measured ability, the Hispanic-coded group is more likely to attend college residentially. Because the file contains no direct BA-completion variable, all conclusions concern "college attendance/completion proxied by dormitory residence," not verified degree receipt.

CORE EVIDENCE — coefficient-change table (Model 1 = SES + race + sex + age; Model 2 = + academic controls; primary complete-case spec, N=3,760, prevalence 17.3%):

Primary spec (ever-dorm any wave 1981–96):
  term              M1 log-odds   M1 OR    M2 log-odds   M2 OR    %atten   M1 p / M2 p
  ses_momgrade        0.147      1.158       0.105      1.110     28.8%    <0.001 / <0.001
  ses_dadgrade        0.091      1.095       0.035      1.036     61.1%    <0.001 / 0.054
  ses_lnincome79      0.210      1.234       0.170      1.186     19.1%    0.001 / 0.006
  ses_famsize79      -0.028      0.973      -0.002      0.998     ~100%*   0.303 / 0.954
  race_black         -0.184      0.832      -0.055      0.947     70.0%    0.294 / 0.769
  race_hispanic       0.409      1.505       1.072      2.920   amplified  0.001 / <0.001
(* |M1 log-odds|<0.05 → % unstable; family size has no meaningful baseline effect)

Refinement (1) — sensitivity, ever-dorm in 1985+ waves only (N=3,760, prevalence 4.1%): pattern replicates — ses_momgrade attenuates 28% (0.159→0.114, still p=0.011), ses_dadgrade attenuates 69% (0.083→0.026, loses significance), race_black moves from −0.126 (ns) to ≈0 (+0.023), race_hispanic again amplifies (0.390→0.938, p<0.001). Attenuation of SES effects is at least as strong when restricted to sustained later-wave dorm presence.

Refinement (2) — race-label sanity check, group means (cohort1 / cohort2 / cohort3=reference):
  dorm-any: 4.5% / 9.4% / 10.8%; dorm-1985+: 1.1% / 2.6% / 2.4%
  mother's grade: 7.9 / 10.8 / 11.6; father's grade: 8.3 / 10.2 / 11.8
  ln income79: 9.13 / 8.96 / 9.34; family size: 4.9 / 5.0 / 3.8
  ASVAB-AR (std.): −0.33 / −0.58 / +0.36; rank percentile: 0.47 / 0.44 / 0.54
  Note: cohort1 has by far the lowest parental SES and largest families (consistent with a disadvantaged group), but its mean ASVAB exceeds cohort2's — a pattern that departs from documented NLSY79 norms (Black respondents typically score lowest on AFQT/ASVAB), so the possibility that labels 1 and 2 are swapped relative to the metadata cannot be ruled out from the file alone. All race terms are categorical with cohort3 as reference, so coefficient interpretation is unaffected by label identity; reported means allow the researcher to adjudicate.

Diagnostics (refinement 3): all 10 logistic fits converged (statsmodels Logit, maxiter 200). N per model: primary 3,760; sensitivity 3,760; ASVAB-only 7,593 (prevalence 11.1%); rank-only 4,041 (16.6%); median-imputation robustness 8,563 (10.3%). Log-likelihoods: primary −1543.5→−1364.8; ASVAB-only −2274.6→−2012.5; rank-only −1627.1→−1498.2; imputed −2430.2→−2094.4 (all improvements are large, LR-significant).

Robustness: ASVAB-only model (largest academic-complete sample) shows the strongest attenuation: ses_momgrade 40.6%, ses_dadgrade 55.5%, ses_lnincome79 42.1%, race_black 96.2% (−0.224→−0.009). Rank-percentile-only model attenuates SES less (17–25%) and barely moves race_black (−8%), indicating the attenuation is driven mainly by ASVAB-measured achievement. Median imputation + missing-indicator model (N=8,563) reproduces the primary pattern (SES attenuation 42–52%, race_black 92.6% attenuation, race_hispanic amplification), so results are not an artifact of complete-case selection on the ~55%-missing class-rank variable. A collinearity issue (identical ASVAB missingness patterns) forced collapsing to one ASVAB-missing indicator in the imputation model.

LIMITATIONS: (a) No direct BA-completion variable exists in the file; the outcome is a residence-based proxy for residential college attendance — dorm presence likely overstates completion and undercounts commuter students, and 56.7% of 1981 residence values are missing. (b) Class rank is observed only for respondents still in school around 1981 (55% missing, non-random) and is endogenous to prior attainment. (c) ASVAB values arrive on a 165–825 scale despite the "Z Score" label; I re-standardized them. (d) Academic controls are treated as mediators (SES/race → academics → completion), so Model 2 coefficients are direct-effect-style associations, not causal effects; post-1985 wealth/income were excluded as post-treatment. (e) Race labels may be swapped (see group means); findings are stated in terms of coded cohorts with the reference group identified.

Artifacts: analysis/run_analysis.py (executed, produces all tables) and analysis/results.json (all coefficient tables, group means, N, convergence flags).

payload.hypothesis: Academic characteristics (ASVAB achievement and class rank) account for a large share — roughly 30-60% — of the positive SES gradient in college attendance/completion proxied by dormitory residence, and essentially all of the small negative gradient for the Black-coded cohort (coefficient attenuates ~70-96% to ≈0); the Hispanic-coded cohort's positive gradient is not attenuated but amplified after academic controls. SES effects operate largely through measured academic ability. Because the file contains no direct BA-completion indicator, all statements concern attendance/completion proxied by ever living in a dorm/fraternity/sorority (NLSY79 residence code 3, any wave 1981-1996; sensitivity: 1985+ only).
payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_raw.csv (12,686 x 61). Constructed outcomes: ever-dorm any wave 1981-96 (NLSY residence code 3) and sensitivity ever-dorm 1985+ waves. SES block: mother's grade, father's grade, ln(1+family income 1979), family size 1979. Race: cohort1/cohort2 indicators vs cohort3 reference. Covariates: sex, age. Academic block: four ASVAB scores re-standardized (raw values arrived on 165-825 scale despite 'Z Score' labels) + class-rank percentile (1 - rank/class size). Nested logistic regressions (statsmodels Logit): Model 1 SES+race baseline vs Model 2 + academic controls; complete-case primary (N=3,760), ASVAB-only (N=7,593), rank-only (N=4,041), and median-imputation + collapsed missing-indicator robustness (N=8,563). Reported log-odds, odds ratios, and % attenuation; % flagged unstable where |M1 log-odds|<0.05. Group means by racial/ethnic cohort reported for label sanity-checking. All 10 fits converged; post-1985 wealth/income excluded as post-treatment.
